findings.label: A
findings.finding: Caller return errors are used directly as health outcomes. Canceled completed 200 resets failures or establishes recovery; the 250ms operation deadline is not considered when classifying a completed 503.

findings.label: A
findings.finding: Parse, transport and body errors are returned without the required diagnostic bound. Reproduced 8245, 8233 and 8192 byte messages in enabled and disabled modes.

findings.label: A
findings.finding: Per-call copied client overwrites and bypasses supplied CheckRedirect policy, even when that policy itself already prevents a second transport request.
findings.interpretation: Application request means one Client.Do operation, consistent with preserving supplied client policy; wire-request cap versus redirect policy is stated as a contract limit.

findings.label: A
findings.finding: Cancellation tests exclude only already-canceled or errored calls and canceled 503; they do not exercise successful body reading while canceled or operation-deadline health accounting. All candidate checks pass despite A-F1.

findings.label: A
findings.finding: Body-result limits and short read causes are tested, but long parse/transport/body diagnostics are not bounded in assertions, leaving A-F2 undetected.

findings.label: A
findings.finding: Borrowed-client test explicitly expects supplied redirect callback not to execute and checks the original client later; it entrenches policy bypass rather than proving Fetch honors borrowed policy.

findings.label: B
findings.finding: Supplied read-error test uses disabled mode; enabled health-exclusion tests omit HTTP 200 with a read error. Removing only the health classifier err == nil condition survives candidate tests and both probe sets but fails equal reviewer body-health probes.

non_findings: Both pass original frozen probes and current body-read-error health reproduction.
Both use unchanged API, Go 1.22.0 module directive and pinned dependency graph.
B correctly separates successful caller bytes from neutral canceled health, and bounds messages with unwrap causes.
A truncates oversized successful bodies; B rejects them. The README does not specify oversize or partial-result policy, so this is recorded as an ambiguity rather than an additional finding.
A allocates an unused breaker map in disabled mode; it adds no breaker behavior and is only a small optional minimality refinement.
